title: Let Every Day Be Christmas | Sri Daya Mata
formattedMarkdown:
# Let Every Day Be Christmas: A Message of Divine Love

### The True Spirit of the Season
Beloved ones, as we gather together during this sacred season, my heart reaches out to each of you. Often, we think of Christmas as a single day marked by festivities, the exchange of gifts, and the gathering of family. But to the seeker of truth, to the devotee of Paramahansa Yogananda, Christmas holds a far deeper, more eternal significance. It is not merely the remembrance of the birth of Jesus Christ; it is the invitation to give birth to the Christ Consciousness within our own souls.

### The Call to Inner Transformation
To "Let Every Day Be Christmas" means that we must strive to make our hearts a permanent dwelling place for the Divine. In the busyness of the world, we become distracted by outward forms. But the master reminds us that the Kingdom of God is within. When we sit in silence, when we withdraw our consciousness from the senses and place it at the seat of the soul, we find that the light of the Christ is waiting for us there. It is a light that does not fade when the calendar turns, a joy that does not evaporate when the decorations are taken down.

**Story • The Gift of the Heart**

Story: I remember a time when Gurudeva, Paramahansa Yogananda, spoke to us about the nature of true giving. He told us of a simple devotee who had very little in terms of material wealth. This devotee went to the temple and, having no money to offer, simply offered his tears of longing and a single, wilted flower. The ego-driven onlookers mocked him. But Gurudeva said that the Divine does not look at the size of the offering; He looks at the depth of the heart. He explained that if we truly wish to celebrate Christmas, we must offer the Divine the gift of our ego—the vanity, the resentment, and the selfishness that keep us from seeing the Beloved. When we empty ourselves, we become vessels for His infinite love.

### Living the Teachings
How do we sustain this state? It requires constant vigilance. We must be the keepers of our own consciousness. When someone offends you, remember the Christ within them. When you are tempted to react with anger, pause and remember the love that sustained Jesus on the cross. That love is not a myth; it is a living reality, an energy that is available to every one of us if we only turn our attention toward it.

### Concluding Reflections
So, my dear ones, do not let the spiritual warmth of this season slip away. Make a resolution today. Let every day be Christmas. Let every day be a day of giving—not things, but forgiveness, kindness, and understanding. Let every day be a day of prayer, where you retreat into the inner sanctuary of your soul and commune with the Christ light. If you do this, you will find that your life becomes a continuous hymn of gratitude, and you will walk in this world with the steady, unshakable peace of the Divine.
